Explain the pinhole camera model and perspective projection, including how 3D camera coordinates become pixels.
risposta: A pinhole camera uses a tiny aperture so a single ray per scene point reaches the sensor, forming an inverted image and avoiding blur. By similar triangles, a 3D camera-frame point projects as xi=f*xc/zc and yi=f*yc/zc (f the focal length), a normalization onto the z=1 plane. Mapping the physical image plane to the pixel grid adds scaling by pixel density (mx,my pixels/mm) and a translation by the principal point (ox,oy). Grouping fx=mx*f and fy=my*f gives u=fx*xc/zc+ox and v=fy*yc/zc+oy.

domanda: Describe the full camera projection matrix, separating intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, and mention lens distortion.
risposta: The full transformation is u_tilde = P x_w = K[R|t] x_w in homogeneous coordinates. The intrinsic matrix K (upper-triangular with fx,fy on the diagonal and ox,oy in the last column) describes internal geometry mapping 3D camera coordinates to pixels; its parameters {fx,fy,ox,oy} are the intrinsics. The extrinsic matrix [R|t] describes the camera pose, mapping world to camera coordinates, with R a 3x3 orthonormal rotation and t a 3x1 translation; these are the extrinsics. Real lenses add radial and tangential distortion, which can be estimated as extra intrinsic coefficients to undistort the image.

domanda: Explain the camera calibration procedure: estimating P and decomposing it into K, R, and t.
risposta: Calibration estimates the 3x4 projection matrix P by observing an object of known geometry and at least 6 known 3D-2D correspondences (P has 11 unknowns since it is defined up to scale; each correspondence gives 2 equations). This forms a homogeneous system Ap=0, a constrained least squares problem (minimize ||Ap||^2 subject to ||p||=1) solved by the eigenvector of A^T A with the smallest eigenvalue; p is reshaped into P. To recover physical parameters, split P=[M|p4]=K[R|t]=[KR|Kt], so KR=M and Kt=p4; RQ factorization decomposes M into the upper-triangular K and orthonormal R, then t=K^{-1} p4.

domanda: Explain stereo vision: depth from disparity, stereo matching, and the global energy-minimization formulation.
risposta: Stereo infers depth by triangulation from two cameras. For a rectified rig (R=I, baseline b), depth is inversely proportional to disparity: z=b*fx/d with d=ul-ur (high disparity = near, low = far). The disparity map is found by stereo matching; for rectified pairs the search is 1D along the same horizontal scanline since corresponding points share the y coordinate (vl=vr). Window-based matching compares patches along the scanline using SSD/SAD/NCC: small windows capture detail but are noisy, large windows are robust but blur discontinuities and miss thin objects. To improve on local methods, stereo is posed as global energy minimization E(d)=sum data term (e.g. SSD per pixel) + lambda * sum smoothness term (penalizing disparity differences between neighbors).
